g.text: One Cloudflare Worker. A chat agent per customer in a Durable Object, the ledger in Durable Object SQLite,
and credit requests in a Workflow that waits for a human approver. All money math is deterministic TypeScript.
React, served as static assets by the Worker
Chat with the copilot as one of 3 synthetic customers
Side panel: current invoice, credit requests, audit trail
Sandbox id and approver token kept in localStorage
"Reset demo" switches to a fresh sandbox
Approver view for the current sandbox
Approve or reject with a reason
15 scripted questions, graded against the engine
npm run eval:live: runs the set against
Worker cf-billing-copilot on workers.dev (src/server.ts). Every request, in order:
sandbox must exist and the customer
admin routes check the approver token
Durable Object, SQLite. One global instance.
new sandboxes: 20 per IP, 200 in total
Durable Object, SQLite. One per sandbox + customer.
Stores chat history and customer memory: account,
8 typed tools, inputs and outputs validated with zod:
Grounding guard: every amount, percent and count in a
reply must appear in this turn's tool results
(one retry, then unsupported sentences are removed)
Anomaly check runs server-side on every invoice touched
The customer confirms before a credit request starts
Durable Object, SQLite. One per sandbox.
Cloudflare Workflows (AgentWorkflow). One instance per credit request; instance id = request id.
Every step is an idempotent Ledger call that writes its own audit record. The Workflow acts on the
decision recorded in the Ledger, never on the event payload. Expiry is a terminal state with its own audit record.
Billing engine (src/engine): pure TypeScript, no Cloudflare imports
Imported by the agent's tools, the Ledger and the Workflow. Covered by unit tests in npm test.
Rating with graduated tiers, proration by active days, tax once per invoice, invoice build and compare, plan simulation, anomaly detection
(one-day spikes against a leave-one-out median) and credit claim validation. Integer cents with exact fraction math, rounded once per line.
The same code produces the seeded invoices and every figure the tools return.
The LLM never does money math
Llama 3.3 only chooses tools and explains their results. Every amount comes from the billing engine in integer cents, travels as
{ cents, display } validated by schema, and the grounding guard removes any figure that is not in a tool result from that turn.
WebSocket chat, panel reads, new sandbox
list and decide, with approver token
